name: Cursor
shortDescription: Code editor with AI built in that can write and change code across your project.
bestFor: Developers who want AI to write, explain and change code inside their editor
about: Cursor is a code editor built on VS Code, with AI built into every part. It suggests the next lines as you type, answers questions about your code, and its agent can make changes across many files at once.
If you already use VS Code, it feels familiar: your extensions, themes and shortcuts carry over.
useCases: Write new features from a plain-English description
Find and fix bugs
Understand a codebase you didn't write
Refactor and rename across many files
Write tests
features: Tab: smart autocomplete that predicts your next edit
Agent mode that plans and edits across files and runs commands
Chat that knows your whole project
Choice of AI models from several companies
Imports your VS Code settings and extensions

howToUse.title: Download and install
howToUse.text: Download Cursor from cursor.com for Windows, Mac or Linux and sign in.

howToUse.title: Import VS Code settings
howToUse.text: On first start, choose to import your VS Code extensions and settings.

howToUse.title: Open your project folder
howToUse.text: Use File > Open Folder. Cursor indexes the code so the AI understands it.

howToUse.title: Ask the agent
howToUse.text: Open the AI panel and describe the change, for example "add a dark mode toggle to the settings page".

howToUse.title: Review every change
howToUse.text: Cursor shows a diff. Read it, accept or reject parts, and run your app to test.

tips: Use git and commit before big AI changes, so you can undo easily.
Add a rules file with your project's conventions so the AI follows them.
Mention specific files with @ to give the AI the right context.
examplePrompt: Add form validation to the signup page: email must be valid and the password at least 8 characters. Show errors under each field and add a test.
limitations: Paid plans use credits. Heavy use of the strongest models can run out fast.
AI code can look right and still have bugs or security holes. Review and test it.
freePlanDetails: Hobby plan with limited AI completions and requests.
pricingNote: US prices. Paid plans include a monthly amount of AI usage.

name: GitHub Copilot
shortDescription: AI pair programmer from GitHub that works in VS Code and other editors.
bestFor: AI code suggestions in the editor you already use, at a low price
about: GitHub Copilot suggests code as you type and answers coding questions in a chat panel. It works in VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains editors and on github.com.
It has a free plan, and it is free for verified students and teachers, which makes it a good first AI coding tool.
useCases: Autocomplete lines and whole functions
Ask questions about code in chat
Generate tests and documentation
Let the agent fix an issue and open a pull request on GitHub
features: Code completions in many editors
Copilot Chat with knowledge of your open files
Agent mode for multi-file changes
Coding agent that works on GitHub issues

howToUse.title: Sign in to GitHub
howToUse.text: You need a free GitHub account.

howToUse.title: Turn on Copilot
howToUse.text: Go to github.com/features/copilot and start the free plan, or apply for student access through GitHub Education.

howToUse.title: Install the extension
howToUse.text: In VS Code, install the GitHub Copilot extension and sign in with GitHub.

howToUse.title: Start typing
howToUse.text: Write a comment describing what you want, then press Tab to accept the suggestion.

howToUse.title: Open Copilot Chat
howToUse.text: Ask questions like "explain this function" or "why does this throw an error?".

tips: A clear comment above a function gives much better suggestions.
Students: apply through GitHub Education for free access.
examplePrompt: Write a function that takes a list of prices and returns the total with 17% sales tax, rounded to 2 decimals, and add 3 unit tests.
limitations: The free plan has a monthly limit on completions and chat.
Suggestions can be outdated or insecure. Review them.
freePlanDetails: Up to 2,000 code completions per month and limited chat. Free for verified students and teachers.
pricingNote: US prices. GitHub has changed how usage is counted in 2026, so check the website for current limits.

name: Claude Code
shortDescription: Anthropic's coding agent that works in your terminal, editor or browser.
bestFor: Handing bigger coding tasks to an agent that reads, edits and tests your project
about: Claude Code is a coding agent from Anthropic. You describe a task, and it reads your project, makes a plan, edits files, runs commands and tests, and explains what it did.
It runs in the terminal, inside VS Code and JetBrains editors, in the desktop app and on the web. It asks for permission before it changes files or runs commands.
useCases: Build a feature across many files
Fix a bug from an error message
Understand a large, unfamiliar codebase
Write tests and fix the failures
Create commits and pull requests
features: Reads your whole project and plans changes
Runs commands and tests and fixes what fails
Asks for permission before risky actions
Works in terminal, VS Code, JetBrains, desktop and web

howToUse.title: Get a plan
howToUse.text: Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan (Pro or higher) or API credit.

howToUse.title: Install it
howToUse.text: Follow the install steps on Anthropic's website, or install the VS Code extension.

howToUse.title: Open your project
howToUse.text: Start Claude Code in your project folder and sign in.

howToUse.title: Describe the task
howToUse.text: Say what you want and how to check it, for example "fix the failing login test and run the tests again".

howToUse.title: Review and approve
howToUse.text: Read each proposed change and approve it, or ask for a different approach.

tips: Add a CLAUDE.md file with your project's commands and rules.
Ask it to make a plan first for big tasks, then approve the plan.
Commit your work before a big change so you can roll back.
examplePrompt: Read this project and explain how login works. Then add a "forgot password" flow that follows the same patterns, and run the tests.
limitations: There is no free plan. Usage counts against your Claude plan's limits.
Always review changes before you ship them.
freePlanDetails: No free plan. It is included in paid Claude plans.
cheapestPaidPlan: Included in Claude Pro — $20/month ($17/month billed yearly)
pricingNote: US prices. Usage is shared with your normal Claude chats.

name: Replit
shortDescription: Build, run and publish apps in your browser with an AI agent.
bestFor: Building and putting an app online from the browser, with nothing to install
about: Replit is a coding platform in your browser. Its AI agent can build an app from a description, and Replit runs and publishes it for you, with a database and hosting included.
It is good for beginners and for quick prototypes, because there is nothing to install and you can work from any computer.
useCases: Build a website or web app from a description
Learn to code without installing anything
Make a quick prototype to show people
Run small bots and scripts online
features: Replit Agent builds apps from a prompt
Code editor that runs in the browser
One-click publishing with hosting
Built-in database and secret storage

howToUse.title: Sign up
howToUse.text: Create an account at replit.com.

howToUse.title: Describe your app
howToUse.text: On the home page, type what you want to build, for example "a to-do app with login".

howToUse.title: Review the plan
howToUse.text: The agent proposes a plan. Change it or approve it.

howToUse.title: Test and ask for changes
howToUse.text: Try the app in the preview and tell the agent what to fix or add.

howToUse.title: Publish
howToUse.text: Click Publish to put it online with a link you can share.

tips: Start small, get it working, then add features one at a time.
Watch your credit use. Big changes use more.
examplePrompt: Build a simple expense tracker: add an expense with amount, category and date, show a monthly total and a pie chart by category.
limitations: Agent work uses credits, and big projects can cost more than the plan price.
You still need to check security before real users sign up.
freePlanDetails: Starter plan with limited Agent use and public apps.
pricingNote: US prices. Core includes a monthly amount of usage credit.

name: Lovable
shortDescription: Builds full web apps from a chat description, no coding needed.
bestFor: Non-coders who want a working web app or website from a description
about: Lovable builds web apps from a conversation. You describe what you want, it writes the code, and you see the result straight away. You keep chatting to change it.
It can add login, a database and payments, and you can connect it to GitHub to own and edit the code.
useCases: Build a landing page or website for a business
Make a prototype of a startup idea
Create an internal tool, such as a booking form
Turn a design screenshot into a working page
features: Builds apps from chat messages
Live preview while it builds
Built-in database, login and hosting
GitHub sync so you own the code

howToUse.title: Sign up
howToUse.text: Create an account at lovable.dev.

howToUse.title: Describe your app
howToUse.text: Write what it is for, who uses it and the main pages. You can attach a screenshot or sketch.

howToUse.title: Check the first version
howToUse.text: Look at the preview and click through it.

howToUse.title: Ask for changes one at a time
howToUse.text: Small, clear requests work best: "make the header blue", "add a contact form".

howToUse.title: Publish
howToUse.text: Publish to get a link, and connect your own domain if you want.

tips: Plan your pages and features before you start, so you use fewer credits.
Connect GitHub early so you have a backup of the code.
examplePrompt: Build a one-page website for a home bakery in Lahore: hero with photo, menu with prices, order form that sends to email, and WhatsApp button.
limitations: Every message uses credits. The free plan gives only a few per day.
Complex apps still need a developer to review and maintain.
freePlanDetails: 5 credits per day, up to 30 per month.
pricingNote: US prices. Yearly billing gives two months free.

name: v0
shortDescription: Vercel's AI that turns prompts and screenshots into web pages and apps.
bestFor: Making good-looking web pages and UI from a prompt or a screenshot
about: v0 is an AI app builder from Vercel, the company behind Next.js. It is especially good at clean, modern interfaces: describe a page or paste a screenshot, and it builds it in React and Tailwind.
You can publish to Vercel in one click, or copy the code into your own project.
useCases: Build a landing page or dashboard design
Turn a screenshot or Figma design into code
Make UI components for a Next.js project
Prototype an app idea quickly
features: Generates React and Tailwind code
Works from text, screenshots and designs
One-click deploy to Vercel
Copy code into your own project

howToUse.title: Sign in
howToUse.text: Go to v0.app and sign in with a Vercel account.

howToUse.title: Describe or upload
howToUse.text: Type what you want or attach a screenshot of a design you like.

howToUse.title: Refine in chat
howToUse.text: Ask for changes to colours, layout and content.

howToUse.title: Publish or export
howToUse.text: Deploy to Vercel, or copy the code into your project.

tips: Name the style you want: "minimal", "dark", "like a SaaS landing page".
Ask for mobile layout checks before you publish.
examplePrompt: Create a pricing page with 3 plans (Free, Pro, Team), a monthly/yearly toggle, a feature comparison table and an FAQ section.
limitations: The free plan has small monthly credits and a daily message limit.
Best with Next.js and React. Other frameworks need more work.
freePlanDetails: $5 of credits per month, with a daily message limit.
pricingNote: US prices. Reports say the older $20 Premium plan is closed to new users. Check the website.
